impl.summary: Clean the voice first. Requests take a new voiceFirst flag. createGenerations turns it into one batch of steps, so every caller gets it. Open engine: DBS (oss-dbs-separate) runs first, then Qwen3-ASR, InfiniteTalk or LatentSync reads its voice stem. For a lip re-sync of a clip that has sound, the clip is split too, and oss-mux puts the clean voice over the clip's background at 0 dB, with the picture copied. Cloud: ElevenLabs Voice Isolation runs before Scribe v2 or the lip sync model, with no put-back because samAudioCloud is false, and the switch says so. previewGeneration adds the step's price and checks it. The Transcribe, Lipsync & avatars, Captions, Genjutsu 'Use the clip's words' and Character Swap Studio transcript screens each have a switch. It shows the time it adds on your GPU or its price in the cloud. It is on by default for video sources and off for audio-only ones. Already there before this package: DBS graph A, oss-dbs-separate, the STEM_ALIASES voice/background, the oss-mux two-track mux (D2), and elevenlabs-voice-isolation in the catalog. No new graph, model, migration or route was needed.
built: src/lib/av/voice-first.ts (pure): planVoiceFirst gives voice → main → (open lip re-sync of a clip with sound) bed + film steps. Also voiceSource, voiceFirstApplies, voiceFirstDefault (on when the speech comes with a video), putsBedBack, voiceFirstCost (catalog price, or ISOLATION_USD_PER_MINUTE = 0.10 for pages without the catalog; a test keeps the two equal), voiceFirstTime (splitTime, the host's DBS pick, mono; doubled plus the mux with the put-back), voiceFirstLine, and the hint and BED_NOTES copy per engine

src/server/voice-first.ts: voiceFirstPlanFor reads the speech's and the clip's headers through storedMedia, so an account's run sees only its own files. It skips the put-back for a silent clip and the step for a silent recording. createVoiceFirstRun builds a createPipeline batch, puts the result first, keeps the asked request through withAsked (now exported from chains.ts) so Reuse and skills rerun it, and rewords a failing step as 'Clean the voice first can't run (…): …. Turn it off to run without it'

generations.ts: createGenerations expands voiceFirst when nothing waits on it (it also works as a pipeline step, which Swap Studio uses). previewGeneration adds the extra steps' cost and notes and refuses in the switch's words
GenerationRequest.voiceFirst in types.ts, request-schema.ts (zod) and the recipe-builder KEEP list

UI: VoiceFirstSwitch (src/components/studio/voice-first-switch.tsx) has the switch, a hint per engine, the time or price line (under the words on a phone), and for a lip re-sync of a clip what happens to its music and effects. Composer: StudioConfig.voiceFirst on TRANSCRIBE_STUDIO and LIPSYNC_STUDIO. A pick holds per speech file. The probe gives the length and whether the clip has sound. The client cost estimate includes the step, and submit sends voiceFirst

Captions: transcribeRequest({ voiceFirst, seconds }) and the switch under 'Transcribe the speech'. Genjutsu: TranscribeSchema.voiceFirst, the switch under 'Use the clip's words', and the cached transcript is keyed by the switch. Character Swap Studio: planTranscribe(clip, engine, voiceFirst), the route takes voiceFirst, StudioEstimate.cleanVoice holds the added price per clip, and the button's price follows the switch

Live on the CPU ComfyUI (DBSLoader present, both DBS models on disk) through a dev server, POST /api/generations with voiceFirst on an 11 s H.264+AAC clip (JFK's public-domain speech over sine chords and pink-noise bursts): DBS-BSRNN mono took 41 s with the load and gave voice, music, effects and background. Qwen3-ASR 0.6B on the voice stem took 68 s and its transcript was word-perfect. Without the switch the transcript was also word-perfect (17 s), so this clip shows no gain; measuring one is D4's job

impl.docsNotes: STATUS/ARCHITECTURE (left for the docs pass): 'Clean the voice first' (DBS D6). A voiceFirst flag on a generation request runs the speech alone through the transcript or lip sync: DBS voice stem on your GPU, ElevenLabs Voice Isolation ($0.10/min) in the cloud. A lip re-sync of a clip on your GPU gets the clip's music and effects back through oss-mux at 0 dB; the cloud keeps the clean voice only, because samAudioCloud is false. Switches in Transcribe, Lipsync & avatars, Captions, Genjutsu 'Use the clip's words' and Character Swap Studio's transcript. On by default for video, off for audio. Code: src/lib/av/voice-first.ts and src/server/voice-first.ts (expanded inside createGenerations), src/components/studio/voice-first-switch.tsx. The Lipsync studio opens on talking-avatar models (InfiniteTalk, Kling Avatar 2), so the put-back applies only when a re-sync model (InfiniteTalk Lip Re-sync, LatentSync, Sync Lipsync) is picked; the switch is on by default whenever a clip is attached. findings.title: Hosted runs: Clean the voice first's extra steps run on the install's GPUs unpriced and past the pool policy
findings.where: src/server/generations.ts createGenerations (voiceFirst branch) + src/server/hosted-run.ts decidePlace/poolQuote + src/server/hosted.ts runFacts/poolAllows
findings.detail: decidePlace and poolQuote check poolAllows only for planned.model.id (the transcriber or lip sync model), and runFacts sends the billing service only that model, op, jobs and seconds. With voiceFirst the run then queues oss-dbs-separate (and, for a lip re-sync of a clip with sound, a second DBS pass over the clip plus oss-mux) on the same pool. The billing service never sees those steps, and a policy that denies oss-dbs-separate or oss-mux on the pool cannot stop them. The brief says a model or op on that path 'plans and prices there too (poolQuote; test it in the style of tests/hosted-runs.test.ts)'. The implementer's 'left' says 'the DBS step is free', but no hosted-runs test covers voiceFirst. This only happens with FUOBE_HOSTED_RUNS=1 and a policy that allows audio or video uploads (off by default).
findings.verified: Traced: previewGeneration's voiceFirstExtra adds only a USD cost, which is 0 on the open engine. runFacts (hosted.ts:139-165) carries no step list or voiceFirst. poolAllows (hosted.ts:55) is called with planned.model.id only.
findings.fix: In decidePlace and poolQuote, when req.voiceFirst applies, check poolAllows for every voiceFirstPlanFor step model and add the steps to the facts sent for billing (or keep voiceFirst runs on the account's own GPU). Add a hosted-runs test.

findings.title: Lipsync default turns on cleaning of an uploaded voice file, against the brief's 'off for audio-only speech uploads'. In the cloud this costs money by default.
findings.detail: For lipsync the file that gets cleaned is always inputs.audio, which is an audio upload (voiceSource). The default still turns on whenever a clip is attached. On the cloud engine there is no put-back, so the default adds paid ElevenLabs Voice Isolation ($0.10/min) to a voice that is usually already clean (a recording or TTS), and gives no benefit. On the open engine the default also adds two DBS passes. The brief's rule is 'on for video sources, off for audio-only speech uploads'. The bed put-back is a separate benefit that could be decided apart from cleaning the voice. The implementer flagged the choice in docsNotes but did not raise it as a deviation from the brief.
findings.verified: Read voiceFirstDefault, and the composer's voiceFirstOn = vfApplies && (pick ?? voiceFirstDefault). tests/voice-first.test.ts asserts the on-by-default behaviour for a lip sync clip.
findings.fix: Default off for a lipsync voice upload, at least on the cloud engine. Or make the put-back on the open engine its own default-on choice, and keep 'clean the voice' off for an uploaded voice.

fix.finalSummary: Open engine (ComfyUI + ComfyUI-DBS): Clean the voice first runs DBS before Qwen3-ASR, InfiniteTalk or LatentSync, which read its voice stem. With the switch on, a lip re-sync of a clip with sound gets the clip's music and effects back through oss-mux at 0 dB. Verified live on the CPU ComfyUI by the implementer: DBS then Qwen3-ASR, word-perfect. Needs a GPU, not verified: the lip sync with the put-back. The switch is on by default for a video's soundtrack and off for audio uploads, now including the Lipsync voice. A voice already cleaned on upload starts off and says so. Cloud engine: ElevenLabs Voice Isolation ($0.10/min) runs before Scribe v2 or the lip sync model. There is no put-back, because samAudioCloud is false, and the switch says so. Built and unit-tested; the paid calls need a fal key. Unknown step prices now show as unknown. Public sign-up: guests browse the switch read-only. An account's clean-voice run reads only its own files and runs on its own GPU (tests/account-voice-first.test.ts). With hosted runs on, the extra steps are now checked against the pool policy and sent to the billing service as RunFacts.steps, so a denied DBS or mux keeps the run off the install's GPUs. The GPU pre-flight board shows the DBS graph on the new Captions and 'Lip re-sync, voice cleaned' rows.
left: RunFacts.steps is a new optional field in the billing contract (docs/billing-hook.md). A billing service that ignores it prices only the main model, as before.
Still needs a GPU: a lip re-sync with the put-back. Still needs a fal key: paid ElevenLabs isolation.
The default (on for a video, off for audio) is still a guess until D4 measures WER with and without the switch.
